question: Why do nurses check (palpate) peripheral nerves during a leprosy assessment?

options.A: The bacterium multiplies exclusively inside superficial lymph nodes.
options.B: Infected nerves often become enlarged, tender, and thickened.
options.C: Nerve palpation measures the exact systemic white blood cell count.
options.D: It stimulates local blood flow to clear dormant pathogens faster.

explanation: You nailed it! Feeling for swollen or tender nerves helps us spot where the infection is causing trouble. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h3)

question: What is a common mistake nurses should avoid when suspecting a notifiable disease outbreak?

options.A: Informing the local government health team too quickly
options.B: Using standard case definition sheets during patient assessment
options.C: Waiting for full laboratory confirmation before reporting the suspect case
options.D: Submitting weekly summary logs to public health authorities

explanation: Never wait for lab results if you suspect a dangerous outbreak! Report based on clinical signs right away so health teams can act fast. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why do nurses ask patients about how many pads or tampons they use when assessing heavy periods?

options.A: It reveals the exact day ovulation occurred during the previous month.
options.B: It determines whether the patient has reached early menopause.
options.C: It measures the exact size and muscular strength of the uterus.
options.D: It helps estimate the actual amount of blood lost.

explanation: Since everyone's definition of 'heavy' is different, counting pads gives you a practical, objective way to measure blood loss. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h7)

question: A patient complains of a burning, shooting pain down their leg from a pinched nerve. What kind of pain is this?

options.A: Somatic pain
options.B: Visceral pain
options.C: Neuropathic pain
options.D: Acute nociceptive pain

explanation: When the nervous system itself is damaged, it often causes burning, tingling, or shooting sensations. That's classic neuropathic pain! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h2)

question: What term describes the thickening of the skin caused by chronic scratching and rubbing?

options.A: Maceration
options.B: Excoriation
options.C: Lichenification
options.D: Desquamation

explanation: Lichenification refers to thickened, leathery skin markings that develop after a patient repeatedly scratches or rubs an itchy area over a long period. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h5)

question: Which part of the penis directly wraps around and surrounds the urethra?

options.A: Dartos muscle layer
options.B: Corpus spongiosum
options.C: Corpora cavernosa
options.D: Tunica albuginea

explanation: Great job thinking through the anatomy! The corpus spongiosum is the single column of spongy tissue that houses and protects the urethra as it runs down to the tip. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which of these everyday ward items belongs to the general waste category?

options.A: Food wrappers from the ward kitchen
options.B: Used hypodermic needles
options.C: Surgically removed tissue samples
options.D: Expired antibiotic tablets

explanation: That's correct! General waste is non-hazardous and similar to ordinary household rubbish, like paper and food packaging. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h2)

question: A patient with severe bleeding after childbirth is in shock, but blood isn't ready at the bank yet. What should you do first?

options.A: Mobilize family donors for replacement and start rapid IV crystalloids while waiting
options.B: Wait patiently until the blood bank completes routine screening hours later
options.C: Administer strong vasopressors without starting any fluid replacement
options.D: Discharge the patient home with oral iron supplements

explanation: Great nursing judgment! In real clinical practice, we start IV fluids right away and quickly rally family members to donate blood while we wait. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h8)

question: A student spends 12 hours a day playing online games, skips meals, and is failing exams. What does this point to?

options.A: Internet Gaming Disorder
options.B: Acute social anxiety
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
options.D: Normal adolescent recreation

explanation: When gaming takes over someone's entire life and basic needs or responsibilities get ignored, it goes way beyond normal fun and fits Internet Gaming Disorder. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T14#GNS312_U3_T14_h2)

question: What is a defining characteristic of a modern intensive care unit?

options.A: Low staffing levels because patients are mostly stable
options.B: High nurse-to-patient ratios and specialized life support equipment
options.C: Large open wards with minimal monitoring equipment
options.D: Focus primarily on long-term physical therapy and recovery

explanation: ICUs require specialized equipment and close nursing watch due to the extreme instability of the patients admitted there. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h3)

question: Besides the risk of physical infection, what immediate emotional impact does a needle-stick injury often have on a nurse?

options.A: Complete temporary paralysis of the affected hand
options.B: Immediate dismissal from their nursing position
options.C: Automatic immunity to all future bloodborne viruses
options.D: Severe psychological stress and anxiety while waiting for test results

explanation: So true. Waiting for screening results after a needle poke can cause a lot of worry and sleepless nights. That's why prevention is always your best friend! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h6)

question: As a night nurse, what is the best way to help reduce environmental stress for patients on a busy ward?

options.A: Leave the overhead fluorescent lights on so staff can monitor safely
options.B: Turn up the monitor alarm volumes so they can be heard down the hall
options.C: Cluster nursing care activities to allow longer periods of uninterrupted sleep
options.D: Encourage visitors to stay past visiting hours to keep spirits high

explanation: By grouping your tasks together (like doing vitals and giving meds at the same time), you let patients sleep peacefully without waking them up every hour. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h7)

question: A patient starts coughing violently and turns pale while you are inserting a feeding tube. What should you do first?

options.A: Push the tube in faster to get it past the vocal cords
options.B: Give the patient a large cup of cold water to drink
options.C: Listen with your stethoscope over the left chest wall
options.D: Pull the tube back immediately because it is in the airway

explanation: Coughing and color changes indicate the tube has entered the trachea, requiring immediate withdrawal to restore breathing. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the main way functional nursing is organized?

options.A: Allowing patients to manage their own treatments without staff help
options.B: Giving one registered nurse total 24-hour responsibility for a single patient
options.C: Assigning specific tasks like medication administration to different staff members
options.D: Having a team leader direct nurse aides to bathe patients

explanation: Functional nursing divides the work by jobs: one person does all dressings, another gives all meds. It's like a production line! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T3#GNS123_U1_T3_h4)

question: If you absolutely must recap a used needle, what is the safest technique to use?

options.A: The one-handed scoop technique
options.B: Holding the cap tightly in the palm of your hand
options.C: Pushing the needle directly into the cap using both hands
options.D: Asking a colleague to hold the cap while you insert the needle

explanation: Brilliant! The one-handed scoop method keeps your free hand safely away from the sharp tip so you don't accidentally poke yourself. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is the most common heart rhythm seen when a child goes into cardiac arrest?

options.A: Atrial fibrillation with rapid response
options.B: Pulseless ventricular tachycardia
options.C: Ventricular fibrillation
options.D: Asystole or pulseless electrical activity

explanation: Unlike adults who often arrest with a shockable rhythm like VF, children usually arrest after a long period of low oxygen, leading straight to asystole or PEA. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h7)

question: What should a nurse do when family members demand full resuscitation, but the patient has a valid, documented DNR (Do Not Resuscitate) order?

options.A: Call the police immediately to remove the family
options.B: Hide the medical chart so the family cannot see it
options.C: Ignore the DNR and follow the family's verbal demands
options.D: Uphold the patient's documented wishes while providing compassionate support to the family

explanation: The patient's legally documented wishes always come first. At the same time, we support the grieving family with empathy and clear communication. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h5)

question: As a nurse, what is our main goal when trying to stop a secondary injury after head trauma?

options.A: To permanently numb the patient to eliminate all pain
options.B: To reverse the torn nerve fibers caused by the initial crash
options.C: To prevent further cell death by maintaining oxygen and blood flow
options.D: To repair fractured skull bones without surgery

explanation: Well done! Since we can't always undo the initial impact, our nursing care focuses heavily on keeping oxygen and blood flowing so swelling doesn't destroy more brain cells. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T13#GNS222_U3_T13_h2)

question: Which bacteria is most famous for causing fast, painful infections after a cat or dog bite?

options.A: Pasteurella multocida
options.B: Clostridium tetani
options.C: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.D: Escherichia coli

explanation: Pasteurella lives happily in cat and dog mouths. Once introduced through a bite, it quickly causes sharp pain, redness, and swelling. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T11#GNS221_U3_T11_h2)

question: A nurse notices that a physiotherapist and a doctor gave opposite advice on how a patient should walk. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Clarify the care plan by communicating with both professionals
options.B: Follow the physician's advice and ignore the physical therapist
options.C: Discontinue all mobility exercises until next week
options.D: Allow the patient to decide which professional to listen to

explanation: As a nurse, you are the communication bridge! Talk to both team members to clear up the confusion and keep the patient safe. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T7#GNS321_U3_T7_h8)

question: A patient with a history of a previous heart attack is receiving counseling on diet and taking prescribed statins. Which level of prevention does this care represent?

options.A: Primary prevention
options.B: Tertiary prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Quaternary prevention

explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early diagnosis, prompt medical treatment, and lifestyle changes to halt disease progression in someone who already has a condition. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h1)

question: Why do nurses keep doing frequent neuro checks for unstable patients?

options.A: To catch early signs of rising intracranial pressure
options.B: To ensure the patient stays awake all night long
options.C: To keep the patient's family members from worrying
options.D: To prevent the patient from asking too many questions

explanation: Things can change fast in acute care. Frequent checks help you catch warning signs of pressure in the brain early, way before serious damage happens. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why must nurses apply lubricating eye drops to an unconscious patient who cannot close their eyelids?

options.A: To test the corneal blink reflex every hour
options.B: To prevent corneal drying, ulceration, and infection
options.C: To decrease pressure inside the eyeball
options.D: To stimulate the optic nerve and improve brain activity

explanation: Spot on! Without natural blinking, the eye surface dries out quickly, so artificial tears protect the eyes from painful ulcers. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T5#GNS221_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the main difference between gray matter and white matter in the spinal cord?

options.A: Gray matter contains nerve cell bodies, while white matter contains myelinated fiber tracts
options.B: Gray matter is found only in the neck, while white matter is found in the lower back
options.C: Gray matter is on the outside, while white matter is on the inside
options.D: Gray matter carries motor signals, while white matter carries sensory signals only

explanation: Think of gray matter as the processing hubs (cell bodies) and white matter as the insulated highway cables (myelinated tracts) traveling up and down. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h3)

question: As a nurse, why should you look at growth trends over time rather than just a single weight check?

options.A: A single measurement cannot show whether a teen is following their expected growth curve.
options.B: Single measurements are legally invalid for minors in healthcare settings.
options.C: Scales in clinics are rarely calibrated for adolescent body weights.
options.D: Weight changes too slowly to be measured during a routine annual checkup.

explanation: Spot on! Checking weight across multiple visits helps you spot sudden jumps or drops that might signal a health or nutrition issue. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is the medical term for a deep bone infection that can happen if a bite goes all the way down to the bone?

options.A: Cellulitis
options.B: Tenosynovitis
options.C: Fasciitis
options.D: Osteomyelitis

explanation: Osteomyelitis means an infection has reached the bone and bone marrow. It's a serious complication we try to prevent with prompt wound care and antibiotics. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T11#GNS221_U3_T11_h6)

question: What is a major benefit of primary nursing for patients?

options.A: Increased feelings of safety and better communication with a consistent nurse
options.B: Shorter waiting times in the hospital cafeteria
options.C: Elimination of all physical pain within twenty-four hours of admission
options.D: Guaranteed zero hospital bills upon discharge

explanation: Patients love seeing a familiar, caring face every day! It builds trust and cuts down the anxiety of hospital stays. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T3#GNS123_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of the National Drug Policy in Nigeria?

options.A: To ensure medicines are safe, effective, and properly used
options.B: To give nurses the sole legal power to write prescriptions
options.C: To make every single medication free for all citizens
options.D: To stop all foreign pharmaceutical companies from importing drugs

explanation: The policy sets standards to protect the public by regulating drug quality, distribution, and rational use. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h1)

question: A patient notices he cannot get an erection anymore shortly after starting a new blood pressure drug. How would you classify this?

options.A: As an age-related normal variant
options.B: As a secondary sexual dysfunction
options.C: As a primary sexual dysfunction
options.D: As an inherited congenital anomaly

explanation: Spot on! Because his sexual function was fine before starting the medication, this is classified as a secondary issue tied to the new drug. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T27#GNS312_U1_T27_h2)

question: What does an Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) test actually measure?

options.A: The exact speed of blood rushing through the neck veins
options.B: The total percentage of cholesterol in the main aorta
options.C: How much oxygen is trapped in the toe capillaries
options.D: Comparing blood pressure in the ankle to the arm

explanation: The ABI is a quick, painless check where we divide the blood pressure at the ankle by the pressure in the arm to check for blocked leg arteries. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T11#GNS213_U1_T11_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of regulatory bodies like the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria?

options.A: To manage the commercial business accounts of private hospitals
options.B: To protect the public by ensuring safe and competent nursing practice
options.C: To manufacture pharmaceutical drugs for local distribution
options.D: To decide which political party wins national health elections

explanation: Spot on! Professional councils exist primarily to keep the public safe by setting high educational and ethical standards for all practicing nurses. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)

question: Your patient on a nasal cannula complains of a dry, sore throat and a mild nosebleed. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Increase the oxygen flow rate to flush the nasal passages
options.B: Recommend adding humidification to the oxygen setup as prescribed
options.C: Remove the oxygen permanently and document refusal of care
options.D: Switch the patient to a tight-fitting non-rebreather mask

explanation: Dry medical gas can be tough on delicate mucous membranes. Adding moisture (humidification) is the perfect fix to soothe that dryness and irritation. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T9#GNS212_U2_T9_h6)

question: Why do many patients with severe Korsakoff syndrome eventually need assisted living or structured care?

options.A: Severe chronic pain requires round-the-clock narcotic management
options.B: Patients require constant intravenous antibiotics for infections
options.C: Continuous physical therapy is needed to reverse limb paralysis
options.D: Inability to form new memories makes independent daily living unsafe

explanation: Because they cannot safely remember new instructions or manage daily tasks on their own, a structured, supportive environment keeps them safe. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T8#GNS222_U4_T8_h9)

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention in neurological nursing?

options.A: To rehabilitate a patient after a massive stroke
options.B: To cure advanced stages of Alzheimer's disease
options.C: To stop a neurological disease before it starts
options.D: To detect brain tumors through early screening tests

explanation: Think of primary prevention as your shield. It focuses entirely on health promotion and stopping conditions from developing in the first place. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T24#GNS222_U3_T24_h2)

question: What must you always check regarding traction weights during patient care?

options.A: Ensure they hang freely without touching the floor
options.B: Remove them every hour to let the muscles rest
options.C: Increase the weight if the patient complains of pain
options.D: Rest them on a stool when turning the patient

explanation: Weights must hang completely free! If they touch the floor or bed, the pulling force stops working. Simple check, big impact. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T8#GNS221_U1_T8_h4)

question: What main body part does a doctor look at during a laryngoscopy?

options.A: The esophagus
options.B: The bronchioles
options.C: The stomach
options.D: The larynx

explanation: Spot on! Laryngoscopy is all about checking out the larynx and vocal cords so doctors can see what's happening or help with breathing tubes. You've got this! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T4#GNS221_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of looking at clinical signs in tummy (gastrointestinal) problems?

options.A: To calculate the total hospital bill for the patient
options.B: To replace all lab tests and scans completely
options.C: To guess the exact day the patient will leave the hospital
options.D: To give us clues about how well the gut is working and looking

explanation: Signs and symptoms act like windows into the digestive tract, helping nurses and doctors figure out what is going wrong inside. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h1)

question: What common blood collection mistake can make a patient's potassium level look falsely high on a lab report?

options.A: Hemolysis of the blood sample
options.B: Using a small gauge needle for a deep vein
options.C: Leaving the tourniquet on for too short a time
options.D: Storing the sample inside a warm incubator

explanation: Spot on! If red blood cells break open (hemolyze) during a rough blood draw, they spill their inner potassium into the sample, giving a fake high reading. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T9#GNS123_U2_T9_h5)

question: What main change happens inside the tiny air sacs (alveoli) during pneumonia?

options.A: The walls permanently stretch and lose stretchiness.
options.B: Blood flow to the lungs completely stops overnight.
options.C: Fluid, pus, and cellular debris fill up the spaces.
options.D: The breathing tubes stretch out and trap air.

explanation: As the body fights the infection, fluid and white blood cells flood the alveoli. That's why air has such a hard time getting in! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the main difference between an intermittent fever and a remittent fever?

options.A: Remittent causes chills, while intermittent only causes sweating
options.B: Remittent only happens at night, while intermittent has no schedule
options.C: Intermittent drops back to normal daily, while remittent stays high even though it fluctuates
options.D: Intermittent lasts for weeks, while remittent goes away in hours

explanation: Well done! The big clue is whether the temperature touches the normal baseline at least once during the day. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T6#GNS123_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which of these symptoms should you teach a pregnant woman to report immediately as a danger sign?

options.A: Vaginal bleeding at any stage of pregnancy
options.B: Increased frequency of urination in the third trimester
options.C: Mild swelling of the ankles at the end of the day
options.D: Occasional mild heartburn after eating heavy meals

explanation: Vaginal bleeding is never normal during pregnancy and can point to serious issues like placenta previa or a miscarriage. Teaching mothers these danger signs saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T015#GNS226_U1_T015_h7)

question: How does COVID-19 mostly spread from person to person?

options.A: By drinking contaminated municipal water supplies
options.B: Through the bite of infected mosquitoes and ticks
options.C: By consuming undercooked poultry and beef products
options.D: Through respiratory droplets from coughing and talking

explanation: You got it! Tiny droplets released into the air when people talk, cough, or sneeze are the main way the virus travels. Simple infection control basics! [learn more](GNS123_U4_T6#GNS123_U4_T6_h2)

question: A child comes in with chest retractions, nasal flaring, and breathing very fast. Which part of the Pediatric Assessment Triangle does this show?

options.A: Circulation to the skin
options.B: Work of breathing
options.C: Appearance
options.D: Neurological status

explanation: Spotting retractions and nasal flaring tells you right away how hard the child is working to pull air in. That's all about their work of breathing! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h1)

question: A mother exclusively breastfeeding her four-month-old baby notices her monthly period just returned. What should you advise her about LAM?

options.A: Her body is just adjusting and she is still fully protected from pregnancy
options.B: She should stop breastfeeding immediately to restore protection
options.C: She can continue relying on LAM safely until the baby is one year old
options.D: LAM is no longer reliable, and she should add another family planning method

explanation: The return of her monthly period means her body's fertility cycle has woken back up. Time to introduce a backup family planning method! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T009#GNS226_U6_T009_h5)

question: What is the go-to, first-line drug recommended to prevent postpartum haemorrhage right after delivery?

options.A: Nifedipine
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Hydralazine
options.D: Magnesium sulfate

explanation: Oxytocin is our superstar drug here! It safely helps the uterus contract down firmly to keep heavy bleeding away. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h4)

question: What is the main goal of hormone therapy in certain cancers?

options.A: To permanently increase the patient's natural testosterone and estrogen levels
options.B: To block or lower hormone levels that stimulate the growth of hormone-sensitive tumors
options.C: To completely replace failing endocrine glands throughout the entire body
options.D: To stimulate rapid production of red blood cells to prevent severe anemia

explanation: Exactly! Some cancers love hormones to grow. Hormone therapy cuts off that fuel supply to slow them down. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T9#GNS321_U1_T9_h4)

question: During a vasectomy, which main tube is cut or blocked to stop sperm from leaving?

options.A: The vas deferens
options.B: The seminal vesicles
options.C: The seminiferous tubules
options.D: The epididymis

explanation: You got this! The vas deferens is the muscular tube that carries sperm from the testes, making it the exact target for this procedure. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h1)

question: How does benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) cause urinary symptoms in older men?

options.A: By increasing the total daily production of urine
options.B: By stopping the bladder muscle from ever contracting
options.C: By squeezing the urethra and blocking urine flow
options.D: By destroying the nephrons in both kidneys

explanation: As the prostate grows larger, it presses against the urethra like a clamp, making it harder for urine to flow out smoothly. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h3)

question: Why is a flatus tube generally left in place for only a short period, such as 20 to 30 minutes?

options.A: To ensure the tube does not dissolve inside the bowel
options.B: To prevent the kidneys from stopping urine output
options.C: To prevent pressure damage to the delicate rectal lining
options.D: To stop the patient from drinking too much water

explanation: Prolonged pressure from an indwelling tube can compromise blood flow to the rectal mucosa, leading to irritation, ulceration, or necrosis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h5)

question: Why is natural daylight or color-corrected light best when checking a patient's skin?

options.A: It eliminates the need to wear protective examination gloves
options.B: It magnifies tiny skin lesions without needing specialized glass tools
options.C: It prevents misinterpreting subtle color changes like jaundice or cyanosis
options.D: It ensures the patient stays warm during a full physical examination

explanation: Yellow room lights can trick your eyes, making it hard to spot important color changes like yellow skin (jaundice) or a bluish tint (cyanosis). [learn more](GNS213_U5_T2#GNS213_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why might a patient complain of right shoulder pain after a liver biopsy?

options.A: Muscle strain from keeping their hand behind their head
options.B: Mild irritation traveling down from the bladder
options.C: A nearby nerve (the phrenic nerve) gets slightly irritated, causing referred pain
options.D: The nurse pulled their arm too hard during positioning

explanation: Correct! The phrenic nerve shares pathways with the liver area, so irritation near the liver can trick the brain into feeling pain up in the right shoulder. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h6)

question: What is the main difference between physical dependence on a drug and psychological addiction?

options.A: Addiction stops the moment you lower the dose
options.B: Dependence only happens to people who abuse drugs
options.C: Dependence is a normal body adaptation, while addiction involves strong cravings
options.D: Dependence stops future pain relief from working

explanation: Physical dependence just means your body gets used to a medicine and reacts if you stop too fast. Addiction is a brain disease marked by compulsive cravings and loss of control. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T2#GNS123_U3_T2_h5)

question: How does a typical resting tremor look in a patient with early Parkinson's disease?

options.A: As rhythmic head nodding that worsens only during high-stress situations
options.B: As violent shaking of both arms when reaching out to grab an object
options.C: As a pill-rolling movement of the thumb and forefinger when the hand is relaxed
options.D: As sudden muscle jerks throughout the entire body during deep sleep

explanation: Picture someone gently rolling a tiny pill back and forth between their thumb and index finger while resting—that's the classic Parkinson's resting tremor! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T4#GNS222_U4_T4_h2)

question: How should a nurse best respond when a palliative patient expresses deep anger about their illness?

options.A: Remind them that anger will only make their physical pain worse
options.B: Validate their feelings and provide a safe space to vent
options.C: Immediately leave the room to avoid confrontation
options.D: Tell the patient to remain positive for the sake of the family

explanation: Anger is a normal response to losing control and health; listening without judgment helps the patient process these heavy emotions. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h3)

question: What is a very common emotional worry for patients facing a terminal diagnosis?

options.A: Excitement about trying new experimental diets
options.B: Fear of becoming a burden to loved ones
options.C: Desire to return to full-time strenuous employment
options.D: Indifference toward family relationships

explanation: Patients with serious illnesses often carry a heavy heart, worrying about the physical, emotional, and financial strain they might put on their family. Empathy is our greatest tool! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T11#GNS321_U4_T11_h4)

question: In critical care, why do we need constant monitoring alongside regular physical checks?

options.A: Doctors rarely visit the intensive care unit more than once a day
options.B: Physical assessments are completely useless in critical care
options.C: Hospital accreditation standards legally demand constant monitoring
options.D: They experience rapid and unpredictable physiological shifts

explanation: Critical care patients can change in a matter of minutes! Continuous monitoring helps you catch hidden trouble early before it becomes a bigger crisis. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T3#GNS321_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which lab result strongly suggests that a bile duct is blocked?

options.A: Decreased serum potassium levels
options.B: Low white blood cell count
options.C: Elevated serum bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
options.D: Increased red blood cell mass

explanation: Great job! When bile cannot flow out, these specific liver enzymes and bilirubin spill over into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of a physical comfort measure used in nursing care?

options.A: Teaching the patient slow, deep abdominal breathing
options.B: Applying a warm compress to a sore, stiff muscle
options.C: Playing soft background music to distract from worry
options.D: Guiding the patient through a mental visualization exercise

question: Why are new mums at higher risk for their bladder becoming too full after giving birth?

question: What is the most common way people get poisoned right inside their own homes?

question: How soon can a woman theoretically start ovulating again after experiencing an abortion?

question: A lucid adult patient refuses to take their morning drugs. What should you do first?

question: Why is noting the exact time of death so crucial for the healthcare team?

question: When should you, as the nurse, do your final dosage calculation?

question: Which of these protects an older adult's mental health?

question: Which of the following is NOT an early sign of respiratory distress or hypoxia?

question: Which action represents a direct breach of client confidentiality in a family planning clinic?

question: During which stage of an infection does a patient feel just a bit 'off' with vague, mild symptoms, yet they easily spread the illness to others because they're still walking around?

question: Which hormone surge directly triggers ovulation around day 14 of the cycle?

question: What does the term 'stricture' mean when talking about urinary tract injuries?

question: What is the main purpose of denial when a patient first receives a terminal diagnosis?

question: How do global health organizations view female genital mutilation?

question: Besides normal vital signs, what else must a nurse check during a rehab assessment?

question: Why is it a big mistake to make someone vomit after they swallow a corrosive chemical (like strong acid)?

question: Why is good communication especially important before doing a vulvar swab?

question: What is the main purpose of 'informed choice' in nursing practice?

question: Why are degenerative neurological disorders considered irreversible?

question: What food safety rule is most important for a patient with a severely weakened immune system?

question: What is the best diagnostic test for looking directly at stomach ulcers and taking tiny tissue samples?

question: A patient had a deep cut on their shin stitched 8 days ago and asks to remove the stitches. What do you tell them?

question: Why are hospital-acquired infections a major concern for nurses using barriers?

question: How can severe emotional stress or extreme physical exercise affect a woman's monthly cycle?

options.C: Watching out for any bad reactions to local numbing meds

explanation: Nurses prep patients, assist during the check, and keep things safe, but prescribing medications is outside the nursing scope of practice. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T2#GNS311_U3_T2_h7)

question: What physical feature is most commonly seen in Cushing's syndrome?

options.A: Permanent low blood pressure and dehydration
options.B: Central obesity with a round 'moon face'
options.C: Dark bronze hyperpigmentation of the skin
options.D: Severe weight loss and profound muscle wasting

explanation: Too much cortisol changes how fat is stored in the body, leading to a characteristic round 'moon face' and extra weight packed around the trunk and upper back. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T13#GNS222_U2_T13_h6)

question: Why must nurses look at the whole person—not just physical symptoms—when caring for palliative patients?

options.A: Physical pain never occurs without accompanying fever.
options.B: Physical symptoms are often worsened by emotional and spiritual distress.
options.C: Medications only work if the patient is sleeping soundly.
options.D: Lab tests can detect all forms of human suffering.

explanation: Everything is connected! When a patient is worried, scared, or spiritually troubled, their physical pain often feels much worse. Holistic care means healing the whole person. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core part of an effective birth preparedness plan?

options.A: Identifying a designated health facility with skilled staff
options.B: Arranging reliable emergency transportation in advance
options.C: Buying expensive decorative clothing for the newborn
options.D: Saving emergency funds for unexpected medical costs

explanation: You got it! Fancy baby clothes are nice, but true emergency readiness focuses on transport, money, and skilled hands to help deliver safely. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h7)

question: A family member is sitting quietly at the bedside crying after a loss. What is the most caring nursing action?

options.A: Sit quietly beside the family member and offer a comforting presence
options.B: Leave the room immediately so the family can have complete privacy
options.C: Encourage the person to cheer up by remembering happier times
options.D: Administer a prescribed sedative to help the person calm down

explanation: Well done! Sometimes silence and a warm, supportive presence speak louder than any words can. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T9#GNS321_U4_T9_h6)

question: A patient recovering from bowel surgery starts eating normal food again, but complains of sharp cramps and nausea. What should you do first?

options.A: Give a strong laxative to clear them out
options.B: Pause the food advancement and inform the doctor
options.C: Switch them immediately to total IV nutrition
options.D: Encourage them to finish the meal to build strength

explanation: Cramps and nausea are your tummy's way of saying 'not yet!' Slowing down and resting the gut prevents bigger problems like blockages. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h3)

question: Which blood protein acts like a sponge to hold fluid inside the blood vessels?

options.A: Globulin
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Albumin
options.D: Fibrinogen

explanation: Great job! Albumin creates what we call oncotic pressure—think of it as a magnet pulling fluid back into the bloodstream so it doesn't leak out into the tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h2)

question: Which lifestyle change is a major reason diabetes is becoming more common in Nigerian cities?

options.A: Engaging in heavy manual farm labor every morning
options.B: Consuming excessive amounts of natural spring water
options.C: Increasing daily intake of green leafy vegetables
options.D: Adopting processed diets and reducing physical activity

explanation: With busy city life, more people eat fast, processed foods and move around less. This shift in lifestyle greatly increases metabolic risks. Great insight for community nursing! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is a key responsibility for a nurse working in public health cancer advocacy?

options.A: Organizing community awareness and teaching early detection methods
options.B: Diagnosing cancer stages without the need for pathology reports
options.C: Performing independent surgical removal of malignant tumors
options.D: Manufacturing chemotherapy medications in hospital pharmacies

explanation: Brilliant! Nurses play a leading role in public health by educating communities, spreading awareness, and encouraging early screening. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T3#GNS321_U1_T3_h7)

question: What do we call unintended and harmful responses to a medication given at normal, standard doses?

options.A: Primary drug actions
options.B: Placebo responses
options.C: Therapeutic plateaus
options.D: Adverse drug reactions

explanation: Even when we give the right dose, bodies can react unpredictably. Adverse drug reactions are those unwanted, harmful side effects we always watch out for. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T5#GNS125_U5_T5_h8)

question: What is the primary function of the fimbriae on the fallopian tubes?

options.A: To secrete hormones that stop ovulation
options.B: To block sperm from entering the abdominal cavity
options.C: To catch the released egg from the ovary
options.D: To produce mucus for lubrication during intercourse

explanation: These finger-like projections sweep over the ovary surface to guide the newly released egg into the tube. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h4)

question: Which common virus is most strongly linked to the development of cervical cancer?

options.A: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.B: Herpes simplex virus
options.C: Human papillomavirus
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: High-risk strains of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) are the leading cause of changes in the cervix that can lead to cancer over time. Thankfully, we have vaccines now! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h7)

question: A patient with terminal cancer is stressed about hospital bills and how their children will eat. Which team member is best suited to help with this?

options.A: The attending surgeon
options.B: The physical therapist
options.C: The staff pharmacist
options.D: The social worker

explanation: Spot on! Social workers are absolute champions at helping families navigate financial worries, connect with community resources, and handle practical support. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h4)

question: How many licensed nurses must verify patient identification and blood bag details at the bedside before starting a transfusion?

options.A: Four nurses
options.B: One nurse
options.C: Two nurses
options.D: Three nurses

explanation: A mandatory two-nurse bedside check prevents dangerous clerical errors and mismatched transfusions. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h6)

question: How does the heart first try to make up for a severe lack of red blood cells (anemia)?

options.A: By decreasing the volume of plasma to thicken the blood
options.B: By increasing heart rate and cardiac output to circulate blood faster
options.C: By constricting peripheral blood vessels to raise blood pressure
options.D: By slowing down heart rate to let blood absorb more oxygen

explanation: Since each drop of blood is carrying less oxygen, the heart pumps faster and harder to keep enough oxygen moving around the body. It's working overtime! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T14#GNS311_U2_T14_h5)

question: What is a key clinical marker used to evaluate the success of long-term diabetes management?

options.A: Hemoglobin A1c trends
options.B: Shoe size measurements
options.C: Frequency of dental visits
options.D: Hair color and texture

explanation: That's it! Tracking A1c over time gives a clear, reliable picture of how steady blood sugar levels have been. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h7)

question: Which mask is most important when doing a procedure that generates aerosols on a COVID-19 patient?

options.A: A standard cloth face covering
options.B: A disposable paper surgical mask
options.C: A simple clear plastic face shield alone
options.D: An N95 or higher respirator mask

explanation: That's correct! Procedures that create tiny floating mists require the tight seal and special filtration of an N95 respirator to keep you safe. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T6#GNS123_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is a common misconception about using opioids for pain management in palliative patients?

options.A: They always cause severe allergic reactions
options.B: They stop working completely after the first dose
options.C: They can only be given through intravenous lines
options.D: They will inevitably cause immediate respiratory arrest

explanation: When opioids are carefully adjusted for pain, dangerous breathing slowdowns are rare because the body builds tolerance to that side effect. Don't let the fear of opioids fool you! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T11#GNS321_U4_T11_h3)

question: Why is a severely low-protein diet generally discouraged for patients with nephrotic syndrome?

options.A: It makes the urine completely stop flowing
options.B: It increases the risk of developing diabetes mellitus
options.C: It causes blood pressure to rise to dangerous levels
options.D: It does not stop protein loss and can lead to muscle breakdown

explanation: Don't worry if this tripped you up! Restricting protein doesn't stop the kidneys from leaking it; instead, it starves the patient's body and leads to muscle wasting. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h5)

question: How often should you check vital signs during the first two hours after delivery?

options.A: Every hour
options.B: Every 4 hours
options.C: Once every shift
options.D: Every 15 minutes

explanation: Spot on! Checking vitals every fifteen minutes right after delivery helps us catch sudden bleeding or shock super early, keeping our patients safe. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h3)

question: Which item should be counted as part of a patient's fluid intake?

options.A: An intramuscular pain injection
options.B: An intravenous blood transfusion
options.C: A solid tablet pain medication
options.D: A dry solid piece of toast

explanation: Blood products and IV fluids introduce liquid directly into the vascular system and must be counted as intake. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h3)

question: A patient comes in with ringworm on their arm. What type of germ causes this common skin condition?

options.A: Fungi
options.B: Parasite
options.C: Bacteria
options.D: Virus

explanation: Correct! Don't let the name fool you—ringworm is caused by a fungus, not an actual worm. It loves warm, damp skin spots! [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which systemic autoimmune condition is a common underlying cause of chronic glomerulonephritis?

options.A: Systemic lupus erythematosus
options.B: Chronic asthma
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis only

explanation: Lupus (SLE) is a well-known condition where the body's immune system attacks its own tissues, very frequently targeting the delicate filters in the kidneys. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T5#GNS213_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which IV fluid is the only safe choice to use for priming blood tubing?

options.A: 0.45% Sodium Chloride
options.B: 0.9% Normal Saline
options.C: 5% Dextrose in Water
options.D: Ringer's Lactate Solution

explanation: Stick to Normal Saline (0.9%)! Dextrose can actually make red blood cells burst (hemolysis), and Ringer's Lactate has calcium that can cause the blood to clot in the tubing. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T12#GNS311_U2_T12_h4)

question: Which Nigerian law helps protect people by criminalizing harmful practices like FGM and forced marriage?

options.A: Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act
options.B: National Health Insurance Authority Act
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Registration Decree
options.D: Criminal Code for Infectious Disease Control

explanation: You've got this! The VAPP Act is a powerful legal tool in Nigeria used to fight against violence and harmful cultural practices. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T1#GNS312_U1_T1_h8)

question: What are the main jobs of the large intestine?

options.A: Producing bile and filtering toxins from the blood
options.B: Secreting hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor
options.C: Digesting proteins and absorbing simple sugars
options.D: Absorbing water and compacting indigestible waste

explanation: Well done! The large intestine mainly soaks up remaining water and turns leftover food into solid stool ready for elimination. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h6)

question: When is it legally and ethically okay to break patient confidentiality?

options.A: When a curious coworker asks about a patient's diagnosis
options.B: When family members demand updates over the telephone
options.C: When the nurse wants to gossip about a famous admission
options.D: When the patient poses an immediate danger to self or others

explanation: Well done! Safety always comes first—if someone is in immediate danger of harm, confidentiality rules can be bypassed to keep people safe. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why do nurses stick around and monitor a patient for about 30 minutes after certain shots or vaccines?

options.A: To ensure the patient does not walk around too soon
options.B: To verify that the medication has been fully absorbed
options.C: To measure the exact change in body temperature
options.D: To watch for acute allergic or anaphylactic reactions

explanation: Better safe than sorry! Severe allergic reactions usually pop up fast. Keeping an eye on your patient during that first half-hour means you can jump in with emergency help if needed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h8)

question: A woman who took oral medications for Type 2 diabetes for five years becomes pregnant. How is her condition classified?

options.A: Transient pregnancy hyperglycemia
options.B: Pregestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Secondary placental diabetes

explanation: Because she had diagnosed diabetes and took medications before getting pregnant, her condition is classified as pregestational diabetes. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h2)

question: Why do freshly mixed (reconstituted) suspensions expire much faster than dry powders?

options.A: The active drug evaporates into the air inside the room
options.B: The plastic bottle begins to melt in the refrigerator
options.C: Water activates chemical breakdown and microbial growth
options.D: Refrigeration destroys the chemical bonds of the powder

explanation: Water wakes everything up! Once water is added, it triggers chemical breakdown and creates a cozy home for bacteria to multiply. That's why they don't last long. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h7)

question: Why should a cook use separate cutting boards for raw meat and vegetables?

options.A: To ensure vegetables absorb the flavor of the meat
options.B: To prevent cross-contamination of harmful bacteria
options.C: To keep the kitchen counters looking clean and organized
options.D: To make washing the kitchen tools much faster

explanation: This is a golden rule of food safety! It keeps nasty bacteria from raw meat (like chicken or beef) away from foods we eat raw, like salad. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h4)

question: Why are prophylactic antibiotics usually given within one hour before the surgical incision is made?

options.A: To allow the surgical team time to perform hand scrubbing rituals
options.B: To neutralize any bacteria already present in the circulating air
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing nausea while on the operating table
options.D: To ensure peak tissue concentration of the drug when the skin is opened

explanation: Timing is everything! Giving the drug right before surgery means the antibiotic is fully active in the tissues the exact second the skin opens. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h5)

question: What term describes the emotional and physical exhaustion nurses experience from caring for suffering patients over time?

options.A: Primary bereavement
options.B: Anticipatory grief
options.C: Compassion fatigue
options.D: Somatic denial

explanation: Compassion fatigue happens when caregivers become emotionally and physically drained from continuous exposure to patient suffering. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h8)

question: What score do you give when a patient correctly follows simple commands, like squeezing your hand when asked?
explanation: Obeying commands is the highest motor score possible—a solid 6! It's always a relief to see a patient do this. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T7#GNS222_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is the main heart and soul of palliative care nursing?

options.A: Improving quality of life and relieving discomfort for serious illnesses
options.B: Shortening the natural dying process to reduce hospital costs
options.C: Preventing family members from visiting patients in final stages
options.D: Finding a permanent cure for terminal infectious diseases

explanation: Palliative care isn't about curing a disease; it's about wrapping the patient and family in comfort, dignity, and gentle symptom relief. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T1#GNS123_U1_T1_h8)

question: Which part of your stethoscope is best for listening to bowel sounds?

options.A: The ear pieces
options.B: The heavy bell
options.C: The plastic tubing
options.D: The diaphragm

explanation: The flat diaphragm is specially designed to pick up high-pitched sounds like bowel activity. You're building great clinical skills! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why is it important to test movement and feeling in the fingers or toes below a wound before stitching it?

options.A: To make the skin easier to numb with medication
options.B: To prevent the wound from becoming infected later
options.C: To see if the patient is allergic to local anesthetics
options.D: To check if nerves and blood vessels were damaged by the injury

explanation: Testing distal motor and sensory function helps catch nerve or vessel damage early, before any repair work begins. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why do cancer cells keep growing even after the original tissue injury is gone?

options.A: They receive constant growth signals from nearby nerves
options.B: Scar tissue forces them to keep dividing rapidly
options.C: The body actively pumps extra blood into the tumor
options.D: Their internal regulatory machinery is permanently damaged

explanation: You got this! Inside these cells, the internal control buttons are broken, so they keep multiplying on their own without needing an outside trigger. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T7#GNS321_U1_T7_h1)

question: A patient in skin traction complains of severe leg spasms, and the nurse sees the rope is caught on the pulley wheel. What is the best first step?

options.A: Realign the rope smoothly into the center of the pulley groove
options.B: Cut the traction tape immediately to release all skin pressure
options.C: Administer a stronger pain pill and wait for relief
options.D: Raise the head of the bed high

explanation: You've got this! When a rope slips, the weights stop pulling correctly, which causes muscle spasms. Just pop the rope back into the groove to fix the tension right away. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h2)

question: Why can the withdrawal method fail to prevent pregnancy even when the man pulls out on time?

options.A: Pre-ejaculatory fluid may contain active sperm

options.C: Semen can absorb through the skin of the thigh
options.D: Vaginal walls produce their own sperm cells
